SCOTT COMPANY   PETROLEUM CONSULTANTS</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><a name="s87FFFBB850975C78A8139139FD01FFD0"></a></div><div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">PETROLEUM RESERVES DEFINITIONS</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">As Adapted From:</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">RULE 4-10(a) of REGULATION S-X PART 210</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">UNITED STATES SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION (SEC)</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">PREAMBLE</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">On January 14, 2009, the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) published the &#8220;Modernization of Oil and Gas Reporting; Final Rule&#8221; in the Federal Register of National Archives and Records Administration (NARA).  The &#8220;Modernization of Oil and Gas Reporting; Final Rule&#8221; includes revisions and additions to the definition section in Rule 4-10 of Regulation S-X, revisions and additions to the oil and gas reporting requirements in Regulation S-K, and amends and codifies Industry Guide 2 in Regulation S-K.  The &#8220;Modernization of Oil and Gas Reporting; Final Rule&#8221;, including all references to Regulation S-X and Regulation S-K, shall be referred to herein collectively as the &#8220;SEC regulations&#8221;.  The SEC regulations take effect for all filings made with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission as of December 31, 2009, or after January 1, 2010.  Reference should be made to the full text under Title 17, Code of Federal Regulations, Regulation S-X Part 210, Rule 4-10(a) for the complete definitions (direct passages excerpted in part or wholly from the aforementioned SEC document are denoted in italics herein).</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Reserves are estimated remaining quantities of oil and gas and related substances anticipated to be economically producible, as of a given date, by application of development projects to known accumulations.  </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">All reserve estimates involve an assessment of the uncertainty relating the likelihood that the actual remaining quantities recovered will be greater or less than the estimated quantities determined as of the date the estimate is made.  The uncertainty depends chiefly on the amount of reliable geologic and engineering data available at the time of the estimate and the interpretation of these data.  The relative degree of uncertainty may be conveyed by placing reserves into one of two principal classifications, either proved or unproved.  Unproved reserves are less certain to be recovered than proved reserves and may be further sub-classified as probable and possible reserves to denote progressively increasing uncertainty in their recoverability.  Under the SEC regulations as of December 31, 2009, or after January 1, 2010, a company may optionally disclose estimated quantities of probable or possible oil and gas reserves in documents publicly filed with the SEC.  The SEC regulations continue to prohibit disclosure of estimates of oil and gas resources other than reserves and any estimated values of such resources in any document publicly filed with the SEC unless such information is required to be disclosed in the document by foreign or state law as noted in &#167;229.1202 Instruction to Item 1202.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">Reserves estimates will generally be revised only as additional geologic or engineering data become available or as economic conditions change.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">Reserves may be attributed to either natural energy or improved recovery methods. Improved recovery methods include all methods for supplementing natural energy or altering natural forces in the reservoir to increase ultimate recovery.  Examples of such methods are pressure maintenance, natural gas cycling, waterflooding, thermal methods, chemical flooding, and the use of miscible and immiscible displacement fluids.  Other improved recovery methods may be developed in the future as petroleum technology continues to evolve.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">Reserves may be attributed to either conventional or unconventional petroleum accumulations.  Petroleum accumulations are considered as either conventional or unconventional based on the nature of their in-place characteristics, extraction method applied, or degree of processing prior to sale.  Examples of unconventional petroleum accumulations include coalbed or coalseam methane (CBM/CSM), basin-</font></div><div><br></div><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:8pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;">RYDER SCOTT COMPANY   PETROLEUM CONSULTANTS</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">PETROLEUM RESERVES DEFINITIONS</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">Page </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">2</font></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">centered gas, shale gas, gas hydrates, natural bitumen and oil shale deposits.  These unconventional accumulations may require specialized extraction technology and/or significant processing prior to sale.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">Reserves do not include quantities of petroleum being held in inventory.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">Because of the differences in uncertainty, caution should be exercised when aggregating quantities of petroleum from different reserves categories.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">RESERVES (SEC DEFINITIONS)</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">Securities and Exchange Commission Regulation S-X &#167;210.4-10(a)(26) defines reserves as follows:</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Reserves.  </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Reserves are estimated remaining quantities of oil and gas and related substances anticipated to be economically producible, as of a given date, by application of development projects to known accumulations.  In addition, there must exist, or there must be a reasonable expectation that there will exist, the legal right to produce or a revenue interest in the production, installed means of delivering oil and gas or related substances to market, and all permits and financing required to implement the project. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">Note to paragraph (a)(26):</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">&#32;Reserves should not be assigned to adjacent reservoirs isolated by major, potentially sealing, faults until those reservoirs are penetrated and evaluated as economically producible.  Reserves should not be assigned to areas that are clearly separated from a known accumulation by a non-productive reservoir (</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">i.e.</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">, absence of reservoir, structurally low reservoir, or negative test results).  Such areas may contain prospective resources (</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;text-decoration:underline;">i.e.</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">, potentially recoverable resources from undiscovered accumulations). </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">PROVED RESERVES (SEC DEFINITIONS)</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">Securities and Exchange Commission Regulation S-X &#167;210.4-10(a)(22) defines proved oil and gas reserves as follows:</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Proved oil and gas reserves.  </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Proved oil and gas reserves are those quantities of oil and gas, which, by analysis of geoscience and engineering data, can be estimated with reasonable certainty to be economically producible&#8212;from a given date forward, from known reservoirs, and under existing economic conditions, operating methods, and government regulations&#8212;prior to the time at which contracts providing the right to operate expire, unless evidence indicates that renewal is reasonably certain, regardless of whether deterministic or probabilistic methods are used for the estimation. The project to extract the hydrocarbons must have commenced or the operator must be reasonably certain that it will commence the project within a reasonable time. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(i) The area of the reservoir considered as proved includes: </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:96px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(A) The area identified by drilling and limited by fluid contacts, if any, and </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:96px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:96px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(B) Adjacent undrilled portions of the reservoir that can, with reasonable certainty, be judged to be continuous with it and to contain economically producible oil or gas on the basis of available geoscience and engineering data. </font></div><div><br></div><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:8pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;">RYDER SCOTT COMPANY   PETROLEUM CONSULTANTS</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">PETROLEUM style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(ii) In the absence of data on fluid contacts, proved quantities in a reservoir are limited by the lowest known hydrocarbons (LKH) as seen in a well penetration unless geoscience, engineering, or performance data and reliable technology establishes a lower contact with reasonable certainty. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(iii) Where direct observation from well penetrations has defined a highest known oil (HKO) elevation and the potential exists for an associated gas cap, proved oil reserves may be assigned in the structurally higher portions of the reservoir only if geoscience, engineering, or performance data and reliable technology establish the higher contact with reasonable certainty. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(iv) Reserves which can be produced economically through application of improved recovery techniques (including, but not limited to, fluid injection) are included in the proved classification when: </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:96px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(A) Successful testing by a pilot project in an area of the reservoir with properties no more favorable than in the reservoir as a whole, the operation of an installed program in the reservoir or an analogous reservoir, or other evidence using reliable technology establishes the reasonable certainty of the engineering analysis on which the project or program was based; and </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:96px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:96px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(B) The project has been approved for development by all necessary parties and entities, including governmental entities. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:96px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(v) Existing economic conditions include prices and costs at which economic producibility from a reservoir is to be determined. The price shall be the average price during the 12-month period prior to the ending date of the period covered by the report, determined as an unweighted arithmetic average of the first-day-of-the-month price for each month within such period, unless prices are defined by contractual arrangements, excluding escalations based upon future conditions. </font></div><div Reference should be made to Title 17, Code of Federal Regulations, Regulation S-X Part 210, Rule 4-10(a) and the SPE-PRMS as the following reserves status definitions are based on excerpts from the original documents (direct passages excerpted from the aforementioned SEC and SPE-PRMS documents are denoted in italics herein).</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">DEVELOPED RESERVES (SEC DEFINITIONS)</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">Securities and Exchange Commission Regulation S-X &#167;210.4-10(a)(6) defines developed oil and gas reserves as follows:</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Developed oil and gas reserves are reserves of any category that can be expected to be recovered: </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:96px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(i) Through existing wells with existing equipment and operating methods or in which the cost of the required equipment is relatively minor compared to the cost of a new well; and </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:96px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:96px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(ii) Through installed extraction equipment and infrastructure operational at the time of the reserves estimate if the extraction is by means not involving a well. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Developed Producing (SPE-PRMS Definitions)</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">While not a requirement for disclosure under the SEC regulations, developed oil and gas reserves may be further sub-classified according to the guidance contained in the SPE-PRMS as Producing or Non-Producing.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Developed Producing Reserves</font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">&#32;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Developed Producing Reserves are expected to be recovered from completion intervals that are open and producing at the time of the estimate. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div><br></div><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:8pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;">RYDER SCOTT COMPANY   PETROLEUM CONSULTANTS</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">PETROLEUM RESERVES STATUS DEFINITIONS AND GUIDELINES</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">Page </font><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">2</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div></div><div><br></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Improved recovery reserves are considered producing only after the improved recovery project is in operation.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Developed Non-Producing</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Developed Non-Producing Reserves include shut-in and behind-pipe reserves. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Shut-In</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Shut-in Reserves are expected to be recovered from:</font></div><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:96px;"></td><td></td></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:72px;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(1)</font></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;padding-left:20px;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;text-indent:-20px;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">completion intervals which are open at the time of the estimate, but which have not yet started producing; </font></div></td></tr></table><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:96px;"></td><td></td></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:72px;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(2)</font></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;padding-left:20px;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;text-indent:-20px;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">wells which were shut-in for market conditions or pipeline connections; or </font></div></td></tr></table><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:96px;"></td><td></td></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:72px;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(3)</font></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;padding-left:20px;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;text-indent:-20px;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">wells not capable of production for mechanical reasons. </font></div></td></tr></table><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:24px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Behind-Pipe</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Behind-pipe Reserves are expected to be recovered from zones in existing wells that will require additional completion work or future re-completion prior to start of production with minor cost to access these reserves.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">In all cases, production can be initiated or restored with relatively low expenditure compared to the cost of drilling a new well. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">UNDEVELOPED RESERVES (SEC DEFINITIONS)</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;">Securities and Exchange Commission Regulation S-X &#167;210.4-10(a)(31) defines undeveloped oil and gas reserves as follows:</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Undeveloped oil and gas reserves are reserves of any category that are expected to be recovered from new wells on undrilled acreage, or from existing wells where a relatively major expenditure is required for recompletion. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:122px;"></td><td></td></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:96px;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(i)</font></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Reserves on undrilled acreage shall be limited to those directly offsetting development spacing areas that are reasonably certain of production when drilled, unless evidence using reliable technology exists that establishes reasonable certainty of economic producibility at greater distances. </font></div></td></tr></table><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:96px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:96px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(ii) Undrilled locations can be classified as having undeveloped reserves only if a development plan has been adopted indicating that they are scheduled to be drilled within five years, unless the specific circumstances, justify a longer time. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:96px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:96px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">(iii) Under no circumstances shall estimates for undeveloped reserves be attributable to any acreage for which an application of fluid injection or other improved recovery technique is contemplated, unless such techniques have been proved effective by actual projects in the same reservoir or an analogous reservoir, as defined in paragraph (a)(2) of this section, or by other evidence using reliable technology establishing reasonable certainty.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:11pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><font qualify for discontinued operations accounting under financial statement presentation authoritative guidance.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Properties Held for Sale&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Assets are classified as held for sale when the Company commits to a plan to sell the assets and it is probable the sale will take place within &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;one&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; year.  Upon classification as held for sale, long-lived assets are no longer depreciated or depleted, and a measurement for impairment is performed to identify and expense any excess of carrying value over fair value less estimated costs to sell.  When assets no longer meet the criteria of assets held for sale, they are measured at the lower of the carrying value of the assets before being classified as held for sale, adjusted for any depletion, depreciation, and amortization expense that would have been recognized, or the fair value at the date they are reclassified to assets held for use.  Any gain or loss recognized on assets held for sale or on assets held for sale that are subsequently reclassified to assets held for use is reflected in the net gain (loss) on divestiture activity line item on the accompanying statements of operations.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;As of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2017&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, there were &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$5.3 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$111.7 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively, of assets held for sale presented on the accompanying balance sheets.  The balance as of December 31, 2017, consisted primarily of approximately &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;112,000&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; net acres in the Powder River Basin, and is presented net of accumulated depletion, depreciation, and amortization expense.  As discussed above, the Company sold these assets in the first quarter of 2018.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;2018 Acquisition Activity&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;During the year ended &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, the Company acquired approximately &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;1,030&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; net acres of primarily unproved properties located in Martin and Howard Counties, Texas, in two separate transactions which closed in 2018.  Combined total cash consideration paid by the Company was &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$33.3 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;.  Under authoritative accounting guidance, these transactions were both individually considered to be asset acquisitions.  Therefore, the properties were recorded based on the fair value of the total consideration transferred on the acquisition date and the transaction costs were capitalized as a component of the cost of the assets acquired. &lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;During the third quarter of 2018, the Company completed two non-monetary acreage trades of primarily unproved properties, located in Howard and Martin Counties, Texas, resulting in the Company exchanging approximately &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2,650&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; net acres, with &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$95.1 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of carrying value attributed to the properties surrendered by the Company.  These trades were recorded at carryover basis with &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;no&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; gain or loss recognized.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Subsequent to &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, the Company completed several non-monetary acreage trades of primarily unproved properties, located in Howard, Martin, and Upton Counties, Texas, resulting in the Company receiving approximately &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;1,580&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; net acres in exchange for approximately &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;1,650&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; net acres.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;2017 Acquisition Activity&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;padding-left:6px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;During the year ended &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2017&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, the Company acquired approximately &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;3,600&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; The Company finalized the QStar Acquisition during the third quarter of 2017 by paying &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$7.3 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of cash consideration in addition to the initial consideration of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$1.2 billion&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; in cash consideration and the issuance of approximately &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;13.4 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; shares of the Company&amp;#8217;s common stock, resulting in total consideration of approximately &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$1.6 billion&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; paid after final closing adjustments.  The Company funded the acquisition with proceeds from the 2016 divestitures and the December 2016 equity offering.  Please refer to &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;"&gt;Note 13 &amp;#8211; Equity&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; for additional discussion.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Under authoritative accounting guidance, the transaction was considered an asset acquisition, and therefore, the properties were recorded based on the fair value of the total consideration transferred on the acquisition date and transaction costs were capitalized as a component of the cost of the assets acquired. 	<sm:AssetsHeldForSalePolicyTextBlock contextRef="FD2018Q4YTD" id="Fact-890AB1AFF1A1546B99B41998BC3B4A9F">&lt;div style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Assets Held for Sale&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Any properties held for sale as of the balance sheet date have been classified as assets held for sale and are separately presented on the accompanying balance sheets at the lower of carrying value or fair value less the estimated cost to sell.  Properties classified as held for sale, including any corresponding asset retirement obligation liability, are valued using a market approach, based on an estimated net selling price, as evidenced by the most current bid prices received from third-parties, if available.  If an estimated selling price is not available, the Company utilizes the various valuation techniques discussed above.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</sm:AssetsHeldForSalePolicyTextBlock>

style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt"&gt;(1)&lt;/sup&gt;&amp;#160;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;During the years ended &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2017&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2016&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, the Company issued shares of common stock to settle RSUs that related to awards granted in previous years.  The Company and a majority of grant recipients mutually agreed to net share settle a portion of the awards to cover income and payroll tax withholdings in accordance with the Company&amp;#8217;s Equity Plan and individual award agreements.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</sm:ScheduleofSharesSettledRestrictedStockUnitsTableTextBlock>
	<sm:ShareBasedCompensationAndNetProfitPlanDisclosureTextBlock contextRef="FD2018Q4YTD" id="Fact-BC4E5334D32E56409F1F88EA4AFD9C89">&lt;div style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;padding-top:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Note 7 &amp;#8211; Compensation Plans&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt; &lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Equity Incentive Compensation Plan&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;There are several components to the Company&amp;#8217;s Equity Plan that are described in this section.  Various types of equity awards have been granted by the Company in different periods.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;As of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, approximately &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;5.9 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; shares of common stock were available for grant under the Equity Plan.  The issuance of a direct share benefit, such as a share of common stock, a stock option, a restricted share, an RSU, or a PSU, counts as &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;one&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; share against the number of shares available to be granted under the Equity Plan.  Each PSU has the potential to count as &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;two&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; shares against the number of shares available to be granted under the Equity Plan based on the final performance multiplier.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Performance Share Units&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The Company grants PSUs to eligible employees as part of its Equity Plan.  The number of shares of the Company&amp;#8217;s common stock issued to settle PSUs ranges from &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;zero&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; to &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;two&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; times the number of PSUs awarded and is determined based on certain performance criteria over a &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;-year performance period.  PSUs generally vest on the third anniversary of the date of the grant.  &lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The fair value of PSUs is measured at the grant date with a stochastic Monte Carlo simulation using geometric Brownian motion (&amp;#8220;GBM Model&amp;#8221;).  A stochastic process is a mathematically defined equation that can create a series of outcomes over time.  These outcomes are not deterministic in nature, which means that by iterating the equations multiple times, different results will be obtained for those iterations.  In the case of the Company&amp;#8217;s PSUs, the Company cannot predict with certainty the path its stock price or the stock prices of its peers will take over the &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;-year performance period.  By using a stochastic simulation, the Company can create multiple prospective stock pathways, statistically analyze these simulations, and ultimately make inferences regarding the path the stock price may take.  As such, because future stock prices are stochastic, or probabilistic with some direction in nature, the stochastic method, specifically the GBM Model, is deemed an appropriate method by which to determine the fair value of the PSUs.  Significant assumptions used in this simulation include the Company&amp;#8217;s expected volatility, dividend yield, and risk-free interest rate based on U.S. Treasury yield curve rates with maturities consistent with a three-year vesting period, as well as the volatilities and dividend yields for each of the Company&amp;#8217;s peers.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;PSUs issued in 2017 and 2016, which the Company has determined to be equity awards, are subject to a combination of market and service vesting criteria.  These awards are based on annualized Total Shareholder Return (&amp;#8220;TSR&amp;#8221;) for the performance period and the relative performance of the Company&amp;#8217;s TSR compared with the annualized TSR of the Company&amp;#8217;s peer group for the performance period.  The fair value of these PSUs is measured at the grant date using the GBM Model.  Compensation expense for these market-based PSUs is recognized on a straight-line basis within general and administrative expense and exploration expense over the vesting periods of the respective awards.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Beginning in 2018, PSUs awarded to employees include both a market criteria component and a performance criteria component.  For the performance criteria component, the grant-date fair value is equal to the Company's stock price on the grant date, and compensation expense for the performance-based PSUs will be recorded over the vesting period of the award.  The value being recorded will be evaluated on a quarterly basis and may be adjusted as the number of units expected to vest increases or decreases.  For awards granted in 2018, the Company uses relative debt adjusted per share cash flow growth (&amp;#8220;DACFG&amp;#8221;) compared with the DACFG, as calculated by the Company, of its peer group as the performance criteria that is evaluated over the three-year performance period for these PSUs.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The Company records compensation expense associated with the issuance of PSUs based on the fair value of the awards as of the date of grant.  Total compensation expense recorded for PSUs was &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$10.3 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$9.7 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$11.0 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; for the years ended &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2017&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2016&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively.  As of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, there was &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$19.0 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of total unrecognized expense related to PSUs, which is being amortized through &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2021&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;A summary of the status and activity of non-vested PSUs is presented in the following table:&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:1px;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;div style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The number of awards assumes a multiplier of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;one&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;.  The final number of shares of common stock issued may vary depending on the &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;-year performance multiplier, which ranges from &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;zero&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; to &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;two&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The fair value of the PSUs granted in &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2017&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2016&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; was &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$14.0 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$15.5 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$11.9 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively.  The PSUs fully vest on the third anniversary of the date of the grant; however, employees who are retirement eligible at the time a PSU award was granted, vest in each portion of that award equally in &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;six&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;-month increments over a &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;-year period beginning at grant date.  Retirement eligible employees must stay with the Company through the entire &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;six&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;-month vesting period to receive that increment of vesting and any non-vested portions of a PSU award will be forfeited when the employee leaves the Company.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;During the year ended &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, the Company granted &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;572,924&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; PSUs to eligible employees (&amp;#8220;2018 PSU Grant&amp;#8221;).  As outlined in the award agreement for the 2018 PSU Grant, performance measurements affecting vesting are based on a combination of relative performance of the Company&amp;#8217;s annualized TSR compared with the annualized TSR of the Company&amp;#8217;s peer group over the three-year performance period, and relative performance of the Company&amp;#8217;s DACFG compared with its peer group DACFG over the three-year performance period.  In addition to these performance measures, the award agreement for the 2018 PSU Grant also stipulates that if the Company&amp;#8217;s absolute TSR is negative over the &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;-year performance period, the maximum number of shares of common stock that can be issued to settle outstanding PSUs is capped at &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;one&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; times the number of PSUs granted on the award date, regardless of the Company&amp;#8217;s TSR and DACFG performance relative to its peer group.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;During the years ended &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and 2017, PSUs that were granted in 2015 and 2014, respectively did not satisfy the minimum performance requirements.  This resulted in a multiplier of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;zero&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; times and therefore &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;no&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; shares of common stock were issued upon settlement. &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2016&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, the Company issued shares of common The Company and a majority of grant recipients mutually agreed to net share settle a portion of the awards to cover income and payroll tax withholdings in accordance with the Company&amp;#8217;s Equity Plan and individual award agreements.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The total fair value of PSUs that vested during the years ended &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2017&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2016&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; was &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$10.3 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$8.1 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$8.4 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Employee Restricted Stock Units&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The Company grants RSUs to eligible persons as part of its long-term Equity Plan.  Each RSU represents a right to receive &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;one&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; share of the Company&amp;#8217;s common stock upon settlement of the award at the end of the specified vesting period.  Compensation expense for RSUs is recognized within general and administrative expense and exploration expense over the vesting periods of the respective awards.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Total compensation expense recorded for employee RSUs for the years ended &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2017&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2016&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, was &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$10.8 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$10.3 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$11.9 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively.  As of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, there was &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$20.0 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of total unrecognized compensation expense related to non-vested RSU awards, which is being amortized through &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2021&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;.  The Company records compensation expense associated with the issuance of RSUs based on the fair value of the awards as of the date of grant. shares, respectively, of its common stock to its non-employee directors under the Equity Plan.  In 2017, the Company issued &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;8,794&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; RSUs to a non-employee director.  For the years ended &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2017&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2016&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, the Company recorded &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$1.7 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$1.6 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$2.0 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively, of compensation expense related to director shares and RSUs issued.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;All shares issued to non-employee directors fully vest on December 31 of the year granted.  The RSUs issued to a non-employee director in 2017 fully vested on December&amp;#160;31, 2017, and will settle upon the earlier to occur of May 25, 2027, or the director resigning from the Board of Directors.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Employee Stock Purchase Plan&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Under the Company&amp;#8217;s Employee Stock Purchase Plan (&amp;#8220;ESPP&amp;#8221;), eligible employees may purchase shares of the Company&amp;#8217;s common stock through payroll deductions of up to &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;15 percent&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of eligible compensation, without accruing in excess of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$25,000&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; in value from purchases for each calendar year.  The purchase price of the stock is &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;85 percent&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of the lower of the fair market value of the stock on either the first or last day of the purchase period.  The ESPP is intended to qualify under Section 423 of the Internal Revenue Code (the &amp;#8220;IRC&amp;#8221;).  The Company had approximately &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;1.6 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; shares of its common stock available for issuance under the ESPP as of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;.  There were &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;199,464&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;186,665&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;218,135&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; shares issued under the ESPP in &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2017&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2016&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively.  Total proceeds to the Company for the issuance of these shares were &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$3.2 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$2.6 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$4.2 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; for the years ended &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2017&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2016&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The fair value of ESPP grants is measured at the date of grant using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model.  Expected volatility is calculated based on the Company&amp;#8217;s historical daily common stock price, and the risk-free interest rate is based on U.S. Treasury yield curve rates with maturities Plan&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The Company has a defined contribution plan (the &amp;#8220;401(k) Plan&amp;#8221;) that is subject to the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974.  The 401(k) Plan allows eligible employees to contribute a maximum of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;60 percent&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of their base salaries up to the contribution limits established under the IRC.  For employees hired before December 31, 2014, the Company matches &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;100 percent&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of each employee&amp;#8217;s contribution in cash on a dollar for dollar basis, up to &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;six percent&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of the employee&amp;#8217;s base salary and performance bonus, and may make additional contributions at its discretion.  The Company matches &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;150 percent&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of contributions made by employees hired after December 31, 2014, up to &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;six percent&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of the employee&amp;#8217;s base salary and performance bonus in lieu of pension plan benefits, and may make additional contributions at its discretion.  Please refer to &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;"&gt;Note 8 &amp;#8211; Pension Benefits&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; for additional discussion of pension benefits.  The Company&amp;#8217;s matching contributions to the 401(k) Plan were &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$4.9 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$4.5 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;$5.4 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; for the years ended &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2017&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2016&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Net Profits Plan&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Under the Company&amp;#8217;s Net Profits Plan, all oil and gas wells that were completed or acquired during each year were designated within a specific pool with key employees designated as participants that became entitled to payments under the Net Profits Plan after the Company has received net cash flows returning &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;100 percent&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of all costs associated with that pool.  Thereafter, &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;10 percent&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of future net cash flows generated by the pool are allocated among the participants and distributed at least annually.  The portion of net cash flows from the pool to be allocated among the participants increases to &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;20 percent&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; after the Company has recovered &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;200 percent&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of the total costs for the pool, including payments made under the Net Profits Plan at the &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;10 percent&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; level.  In December 2007, the Board of Directors discontinued the creation of new pools under the Net Profits Plan.  As a result, the 2007 pool was the last Net Profits Plan pool established by the Company.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div 	<us-gaap:AssetRetirementObligationsPolicy contextRef="FD2018Q4YTD" id="Fact-F1EF9EA8A6545F26968AC5DC9262D0B5">&lt;div style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Asset Retirement Obligations&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The Company recognizes an estimated liability for future costs associated with the abandonment of its oil and gas properties, including facilities requiring decommissioning.  A liability for the fair value of an asset retirement obligation and corresponding increase to the carrying value of the related long-lived asset are recorded at the time a well is drilled or acquired, or a facility is constructed.  The increase in carrying value is included in proved oil and gas properties in the accompanying balance sheets.  The Company depletes the amount added to proved oil and gas property costs and recognizes expense in connection with the accretion of the discounted liability over the remaining estimated economic lives of the respective oil and gas properties.  Cash paid to settle asset retirement obligations is included in the operating section of the Company&amp;#8217;s accompanying statements of cash flows.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The Company&amp;#8217;s estimated asset retirement obligation liability is based on historical experience in plugging and abandoning wells, estimated economic lives, estimated plugging and abandonment cost, and federal and state regulatory requirements.  The liability is discounted using the credit-adjusted risk-free rate estimated at the time the liability is incurred or revised.  The credit-adjusted risk-free rates used to discount the Company&amp;#8217;s plugging and abandonment liabilities range from &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;5.5 percent&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; to &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;12 percent&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;.  In periods subsequent to initial measurement of the liability, the Company must recognize period-to-period changes in the liability resulting from the passage of time, revisions to either the amount of the original estimate of undiscounted cash flows or economic life, or changes in inflation factors or the Company&amp;#8217;s credit-adjusted risk-free rate as market conditions warrant.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:AssetRetirementObligationsPolicy>

Intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated.  In connection with the preparation of the consolidated financial statements, the Company evaluated events subsequent to the balance sheet date of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, through the filing of this report. Restricted cash includes cash that is contractually restricted for its use through an agreement with a non-related party.  The Company includes restricted cash in other noncurrent assets on the accompanying balance sheets.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock>

	<us-gaap:ComprehensiveIncomePolicyPolicyTextBlock contextRef="FD2018Q4YTD" id="Fact-03A4F5BE8BA35E43A68D53110BA85366">&lt;div style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Comprehensive Income (Loss)&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:16px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Comprehensive income (loss) is used to refer to net income (loss) plus other comprehensive income (loss).  Other comprehensive income (loss) is comprised of revenues, expenses, gains, and losses that under GAAP are reported as separate components of stockholders&amp;#8217; equity instead of net income (loss).  Comprehensive income (loss) is presented net of income taxes in the accompanying consolidated statements of comprehensive income (loss).&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:ComprehensiveIncomePolicyPolicyTextBlock>
